title: Tanvi Patri, 15, Wins U17 Crown in All-Indian Final at Asia Junior Championships
excerpt: The 15-year-old from Odisha beat compatriot Shaina Manimuthu 11-15, 15-10, 15-12 in Chengdu, capping a breakthrough 2026 season that already includes her first international title.
body:
• Fifteen-year-old Tanvi Patri beat compatriot Shaina Manimuthu 11-15, 15-10, 15-12 in an all-Indian girls' singles U17 final at the Badminton Asia Junior Championships in Chengdu, China, on September 13.
  • The second-seeded Patri beat three Chinese shuttlers en route to the title, adding the continental U17 crown to the U15 Asian title she won in 2024 and her breakthrough 2026 season.
  • India retained the U17 girls' singles title for a second consecutive year, following Diksha Sudhakar's 2025 triumph, and also took bronze in the U15 boys' doubles.

Chengdu, China — Tanvi Patri won the girls' singles U17 title at the Badminton Asia U17 and U15 Junior Championships on Sunday, rallying from a game down to defeat compatriot Shaina Manimuthu 11-15, 15-10, 15-12 in an all-Indian final. The 15-year-old from Odisha came back after dropping the opening game to seal her second continental crown, according to a Badminton Association of India (BAI) press release.

A rematch decided in three

The final was a rematch of the All India Junior U19 Badminton Ranking Tournament final in Bengaluru earlier this year, with Patri once again emerging on top. Sixth seed Manimuthu struck first, taking the opener 15-11, but Patri recalibrated quickly — leveling at 15-10 in the second before holding her nerve in a tense decider to close it 15-12.

Manimuthu, the U15 Asian champion from last year, had enjoyed a strong run of her own to the summit clash. She defeated Japan's Yui Itabashi in the quarterfinals and then overcame another Japanese shuttler, Anon Okimoto, 15-13, 15-12 in the semifinals, settling for silver.

Tested early, dominant late

Second-seeded Patri received a first-round bye but was pushed to the limit immediately. She survived a three-game battle against China's Zhou Jing Li, winning 18-16, 12-15, 15-13, then dispatched Japan's Shizuku Kashio 15-9, 15-12. The quarterfinals brought her most commanding performance — a 15-8, 15-8 win over China's Lin Heng Men — before she edged another Chinese opponent, Yu Ying Gui, 15-9, 11-15, 15-11 in the semifinals.

The victory caps a standout 2026 season for Patri. She claimed her maiden international title at the Pontianak International Challenge and won the All India Junior U19 Ranking Tournament in Bengaluru before adding this continental U17 crown to the U15 Asian title she lifted in 2024.

India's junior pipeline keeps producing

Patri's triumph keeps the U17 girls' singles trophy in Indian hands for a second straight year, following Diksha Sudhakar's title in 2025. India also secured a bronze in the U15 boys' doubles through Aaditya Singh Negi and Tanmay Verma, who lost their semifinal 5-15, 10-15 to Chinese Taipei's Bo Lin Ho and Jui En Hou on Saturday.

For Indian badminton followers in the diaspora, Patri's rise is another data point in a deepening junior bench. India's senior women's singles ranks have been thin beyond the established names, and a 15-year-old winning back-to-back Asian age-group titles — beating Chinese and Japanese players, the continent's traditional powerhouses — is exactly the trajectory that produces senior tour contenders.

What's next

Patri's ranking points from Chengdu should push her toward the top of the Asian junior standings. The immediate question is how she handles the step up to the U19 circuit and senior international events, where she has already begun testing herself this year. With the All India Junior circuit behind her, selection for India's junior world championship squads and a transition to senior Badminton World Federation tour events appear to be the natural next milestones.
